title: Shoppers tap things that don't work on your top product page
group_en: What shoppers do on your pages (Clarity)
pass: On the most-visited product page in byUrl, the share of sessions with dead clicks and the share with rage clicks are each at or below the site-wide share (behaviours.deadClicks.sessionsPct, behaviours.rageClicks.sessionsPct).
fails: The top product page has a higher share of sessions with dead clicks or rage clicks than the site average: shoppers tap the product image, size or colour swatch, price or delivery line and nothing happens, then tap again.
validate: From the Clarity snapshot (store's own Clarity, last 3 days): pick the byUrl row with the most sessions whose URL matches a product-page pattern (Shopify /products/, Salla /p, Zid /products/; cross-check with the product URL from our headless visit). Compare its deadClicks % and rageClicks % with behaviours.deadClicks.sessionsPct and behaviours.rageClicks.sessionsPct. If byUrl is null or no product page is in it, mark 'unavailable'. Our headless phone visit of the same page can show which elements look tappable (images, swatches, badges) but are not links or buttons, as a hint for where to look.
action: Open your top product page on your phone and tap everything that looks tappable: images, colour and size options, the price, delivery and payment badges. Make each one do something (zoom, select, open details) or make it look like plain text.
done_when: On the next 3-day snapshot, the top product page's dead-click and rage-click shares are at or below the site average.
why_it_matters: When a shopper taps and nothing happens on the page that sells, some give up before Add to cart, and that is lost sales on your busiest product.
selected_because: Pool had no measurable point; the snapshot's per-page dead and rage clicks show friction on the page that sells, with a fix the owner can test on their own phone.

title: Errors on the pages where people buy
group_en: What shoppers do on your pages (Clarity)
pass: On the product page(s) and the cart page in byUrl, the share of sessions with script errors and with error clicks is at or below the home page's share and the site-wide share (behaviours.scriptErrors.sessionsPct, behaviours.errorClicks.sessionsPct).
fails: Product or cart pages show more script errors or error clicks than the home page or the site average: a button, option picker or the cart itself throws an error when shoppers use it.
validate: From the Clarity snapshot: find byUrl rows for product pages (URL pattern as in SO-CL-01) and the cart page (/cart). Compare each row's scriptErrors % and errorClicks % with the home page row ('/') and with behaviours.scriptErrors.sessionsPct and behaviours.errorClicks.sessionsPct. Presence check: errorClicks above 0 on the cart page is reported even when below average. If byUrl is null, use the site-wide shares only and say per-page data is unavailable. Our headless visit (product page plus one add to cart) logs console errors on the same pages; list any that match.
action: Send this to your developer: the product and cart pages throw more errors than the rest of the store. Ask them to open those pages on a phone, check the browser console, and fix the errors that fire when someone picks an option or taps Add to cart.
done_when: On the next 3-day snapshot, product and cart pages show script-error and error-click shares at or below the home page and the site average, and our visit logs no console errors there.
why_it_matters: An error on the product or cart page can stop the order at the last step, where every lost shopper was close to paying.
selected_because: Script errors and error clicks on the pages that sell are a direct sales leak, decided by code from the snapshot and backed by our own visit.

title: How far phone shoppers scroll on your top product page
group_en: What shoppers do on your pages (Clarity)
pass: Phone sessions scroll at least as far as desktop sessions (byDevice scrollDepth, mobile vs desktop), and the top product page's scrollDepth is at or above the site average scrollDepth.
fails: Phone shoppers stop scrolling earlier than desktop shoppers, or the top product page is scrolled less than the rest of the store, so delivery cost, payment options (mada, Apple Pay, Tabby, Tamara, COD) and reviews lower on the page go unseen.
validate: From the Clarity snapshot: compare byDevice mobile scrollDepth with desktop scrollDepth, and the top product page's byUrl scrollDepth (URL pattern as in SO-CL-01) with the site scrollDepth. If byDevice or byUrl is null, decide on what is present and mark the rest unavailable. Context, not part of pass/fail: our headless phone visit measures how far down the page (as % of page height) the price, Add to cart, delivery and payment info and reviews sit, so the report can say which of them sit below the average scroll point.
action: On the phone layout of your top product page, move the delivery cost, payment options and a short review summary up, close to the price and Add to cart, so shoppers see them without scrolling far.
done_when: Delivery, payment and review info sit above the page's average phone scroll point on our phone visit, and the next snapshot shows phone scroll depth no lower than desktop.
why_it_matters: If phone shoppers never scroll to the delivery cost, payment options or reviews, they decide without the facts that make them buy.
selected_because: Scroll depth by device and page shows whether phone shoppers reach the trust and payment info; the owner can move that content in the admin.
